page.overview:
Who is Baljin?

Born among the Air Nomads, Baljin initially grew up and trained airbending at the Northern Air Temple. From an early point, he realized that he felt uncomfortable in a highly moralistic as well as monastic community, often sneaking out of the air temple to visit other locations across the world. Eventually Baljin concluded that he had no future at the Northern Air Temple, and resolved to permanently leave. An opportunity to do so arose when the young airbender met members of the Guiding Wind, a renegade order and revolutionary movement that espoused a strong commitment to freedom. He thus ran away and joined the group, spending quite some time with them and going on various missions.

Ultimately, Baljin opted to settle down on the independent Jasmine Island, feeling a strong connection to the location and hoping to pursue "his own independent development" without the Guiding Wind, though he remained loyal to the movement's cause. On Jasmine Island, he generally strove to make his life interesting, "mess[ed] about and [did] what he want[ed]", though also helped the locals using his various skills including his airbending. He eventually joined the local security forces, the protectors, seeing it as a way to both assist others as well as live a free life.

At the time of Baljin joining the protectors, the latter were in crisis due to the machinations of Magistrate Emerald, the civilian representative of the Earth Kingdom on Jasmine Island. Emerald was organizing a creeping coup, undermining the island's old power structures to eventually annex it into the Earth Kingdom, though he did so slowly and covertly. The protectors were among the organizations targeted by Emerald, and he managed to gradually dismantle them by replacing them with Earth Kingdom soldiers who could allegedly better defend the islanders. Ultimately, Baljin became one of the few loyalists who remained protectors even as their organization crumbled.

The situation changed when Emerald imprisoned two Guiding Wind revolutionaries, namely Fengying and Sakuru. This drew the attention of the Guiding Wind's leaders, Khandro and Zeisan, who traveled to Jasmine Island to help their followers. Baljin took a special interest in their arrival due to his existing connections to the Guiding Wind, as he had not yet met the movement's leaders and was thus eager to learn from them during their time on Jasmine Island.
